_comment_about_this_file: This is a SNIPPET showing how to register the kanbanr enforcement hooks in
your Claude Code settings (~/.claude/settings.json for user-global, or
.claude/settings.json in a project). Merge the `hooks` object below into
your existing settings — do not blindly overwrite a settings.json that
already has other hooks; add these entries to the SessionStart and Stop
NOTE: real settings.json is strict JSON and does NOT allow comments. The
`_comment*` keys here are explanatory only. They are ignored by Claude Code
but to be safe you may strip every `_comment*` key before saving.
Replace the ABSOLUTE paths below with where these scripts actually live on
your machine (the hooks/ dir inside this repo's skill/kanbanr/). Make the
scripts executable first:  chmod +x session-start.sh stop-check.sh

_comment_SessionStart: Runs once when a Claude Code session begins. Our script prints the
kanbanr board + recent activity to stdout, which Claude Code surfaces as
session context — so Claude recovers the project plan from kanbanr
instead of working from memory. Best-effort: exits 0 / prints nothing if
kanbanr isn't installed or the directory isn't a tracked project.
_comment_Stop: Runs when Claude finishes responding. Our script checks whether the
kanbanr data git repo has a recent commit; if not, it prints an ADVISORY
reminder (to stderr) to record this session's work in kanbanr. It is a
best-effort recency heuristic and never blocks the Stop event (always
exits 0). Tune the window with the KANBANR_STOP_WINDOW_MIN env var.
